postings.title: AI Infrastructure Engineer
postings.description:
AI Infrastructure Engineer
Your Mission
Join us in shaping the future of secure and innovative technologies across space and cybersecurity.
Based onsite at ESA’s office in Frascati, Italy, you will help build the resilient infrastructure that enables advanced AI services, modern data platforms, and digital innovation across the organisation.
From GPU powered environments and Kubernetes platforms to automation, monitoring, and security, your work will play a vital role in delivering reliable, scalable, and future ready capabilities.
Tasks and Activities
You’ll have the opportunity to;
Design, deploy, and operate secure, scalable AI infrastructure across Azure and on-premises environments, supporting the delivery of enterprise-grade AI services and MLOps capabilities.
Build, optimise, and maintain GPU-powered platforms for AI workloads and large language model (LLM) deployment, ensuring high performance, reliability, and seamless service delivery through secure APIs.
Administer and enhance Linux-based environments, Docker containers, Kubernetes clusters, vector databases, and AI search services, driving efficiency, resilience, and innovation across the platform.
Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) solutions and automated CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, enabling streamlined deployment, governance, and operational excellence.
Monitor platform performance, security, availability, and cost efficiency, proactively troubleshooting infrastructure, networking, storage, and GPU-related challenges to ensure a robust and dependable service.
Implement and manage backup, disaster recovery, patching, and security controls, while producing and maintaining clear technical documentation to support long-term platform sustainability.
What We’re Looking For
Ideally, you will have;
University Degree or equivalent in a relevant field.
At least 3 years of relevant experience in this field
Strong experience designing, deploying, and supporting Microsoft Azure infrastructure, networking, and cloud-native services within complex enterprise environments.
Hands-on expertise with GPU-enabled platforms, including NVIDIA technologies, AI workloads, and the deployment of high-performance computing solutions.
Advanced Linux administration skills, with proven experience managing, troubleshooting, and optimising Docker-based and Kubernetes-driven production environments.
Experience deploying and operating large language models (LLMs) using technologies such as vLLM, Hugging Face TGI, Ollama, or similar frameworks, together with knowledge of vector databases and AI-powered search solutions.
Proficiency with Infrastructure as Code and automation tools, such as Terraform, Bicep, or Ansible, alongside experience developing CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps.
A strong understanding of security best practices, including identity and access management, secrets management, infrastructure hardening, monitoring, logging, backup, and disaster recovery strategies.
Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
Why Make the Move?
Make an impact where it matters. Contribute to high profile projects supporting organisations such as ESA, EUMETSAT, the European Commission, NATO and national defence programmes.
Work alongside some of Europe’s brightest minds. Join an international team of experts who thrive on collaboration, innovation and solving complex challenges that deliver real-world results.
Grow beyond a single project. Join a growing international organisation and broaden your experience across a variety of projects and technical disciplines.
Invest in your future. Benefit from ongoing training, mentoring and professional development opportunities designed to support both your personal and professional growth.
Join a company that puts people first. Guided by our values of Integrity, Inspiration, Care and Collaboration, we offer a supportive culture, flexible working arrangements.
Compensation & Benefits
Compensation will be aligned with the successful candidate’s experience, skills, and responsibilities within the role. For positions based in Italy, employment terms and classification will be determined in accordance with the applicable CCNL framework, with the corresponding level assigned based on qualifications, professional experience, and role requirements.
The advertised salary and level range is intended based on the requirements as advertised here. We welcome applications from candidates with a variety of backgrounds and experience levels, and any offer will be considered on an individual basis, taking into account qualifications, expertise, and overall suitability for the role.
Salary – €40,000.00- €50,000.00 gross per year,
CCNL Level: Level 2-1
CCNL Type : Commercio
Equal Opportunities
This position is open to protected categories under Italian Law 68/99 (Rules for the Right to Work of Disabled People) Questa posizione è aperta alle categorie protette ai sensi della Legge 68/99
We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all candidates, irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.
As part of our commitment to providing an inclusive and barrier-free recruitment process, we will provide reasonable adjustments and support to ensure neuro-diverse applicants or those with a disability or long-term condition can be their best during the recruitment process.
About the Group
CS GROUP, a subsidiary of Sopra Steria Group, brings together the complementary strengths of Starion and HE Space, to create one of Europe’s most comprehensive providers of talent, engineering, software and mission-critical solutions for the space sector.CS GROUP delivers mission-critical systems and advanced software that enable safer, smarter and more efficient space operations. Its expertise spans flight operations, space data intelligence and space engineering. Starion provides end-to-end expertise in systems engineering, mission operations, digital engineering and cybersecurity, supporting resilient space capabilities and sovereign European programmes. With more than 30 years of experience in the European space sector and teams across eight countries, we offer exceptional opportunities to work on missions that matter, develop cutting-edge skills, and make a lasting impact on the future of space. HE Space connects exceptional talent with Europe’s leading space programmes. With more than 40 years of experience, it delivers managed services and highly skilled professionals across engineering, science, software, operations and administration. Together with Starion and HE Space, CS GROUP becomes Europe’s principal source of expertise in people, engineering, software and mission-critical solutions, strengthening its position as a leading European space engineering and digital technology partner for the next generation of space missions.

postings.description:
Antenna Engineer
Are you looking for a new opportunity to take your career to a higher orbit? To join an international group with a successful track record in Space Engineering? A job adapted to your career ambitions and in which you could have an impact for the years to come?
We are looking for an Antenna Engineer to join our Service team and work at ESTEC’s premises in Noordwijk, Netherlands.
The role is part of the Radio Frequency Payloads and Technology Division, offering an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of RF and optical communication systems for space applications.
As a member of this team, you will contribute to the design, testing, and performance analysis of advanced payloads, instruments, antennas, and telemetry systems. You will play a key role in cutting-edge projects, tackling challenges in wave propagation, high-speed data transmission, and signal processing.
Drawing on expertise across antennas, RF equipment, payload architecture, and wave interaction, the division supports ground-breaking ESA missions, and you could be a vital part of the innovation that shapes the future of space communications
About the client and location
The European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) is the European Space Agency’s (ESA) base in Noordwijk, the Netherlands. As ESA’s largest test centre, it is responsible for the majority of space technology and spacecraft development through varying phases of production.
Tasks and activities
The scope of work will include:
Analysing and characterising advanced antenna systems for spacecraft, including mini and CubeSats, and other platforms.
Designing and developing innovative antenna solutions, including arrays, reflectors, lens antennas, and active RF systems.
Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to optimise antenna performance at subsystem and system level.
Developing next-generation RF modelling and design tools, including the application of AI and Machine Learning techniques.
Supporting the testing and validation of antennas, payloads, and instruments in both laboratory and operational environments.
Characterising RF material properties across a range of operating conditions.
Contributing to ESA working groups, international workshops, and conferences.
Supporting technology development and harmonisation activities for reflector and array antennas.
Ensuring activities are delivered in line with ISO 9001 quality standards.
Skills and experience
The following skills and experience are mandatory:
Master’s degree or PhD in Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field.
Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of electromagnetic wave theory.
Experience with space antenna architectures and technologies.
Familiarity with RF, mechanical, thermal, and environmental constraints of space antennas, gained through flight hardware or high-TRL R&D activities.
Knowledge of antenna design, manufacturing, and testing processes.
Experience with antenna modelling tools (e.g. TICRA, Ansys, CST) and programming languages such as Python or MATLAB.
Familiarity with antenna testing and measurement systems.
Understanding of high-power effects in antenna systems.
Ability to work independently and as part of an international, multicultural team.
Solution-oriented mindset with strong communication skills.
Fluent in written and spoken English.
The following skills and experience would be highly desirable:
Knowledge of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence applied to antenna engineering.
Experience supporting and coordinating R&D activities.
Why should you apply?
You will have the opportunity to work within leading space organisations across Europe.
We encourage everyone to think outside the box and to push the boundaries of traditional knowledge. This role is an opportunity to join a forward-thinking company and allows for a deeper understanding of the industry.
To be part of a company that values integrity, inspiration, care and collaboration.
Benefits include: competitive remuneration packages; unique career opportunities, including working in other countries; access to training and development programmes; flexible relocation support.

postings.title: Applied Cryptography Engineer
postings.description:
Applied Cryptography Engineer
Are you looking for a new opportunity to take your career to a higher orbit? To join an international group with a successful track record in Space Engineering? A job adapted to your career ambitions and in which you could have an impact for the years to come?
We are currently looking for an Applied Cryptography Engineer to join our team in Windhof, Luxembourg.
You will be responsible for the entire end-to-end cryptographic integrity of the system, from the physical (quantum) layer to the abstract (MPC) and application (PQC) layers. You will act as the key person that guarantees the security of the entire key generation and delivery chain.
About the client and location
Starion Luxembourg provides full lifecycle engineering solutions, including design, integration and operation, for complex programmes. We supply operations and ground system engineering services for missions including Earth observation, quantum communications, scientific, navigation and space exploration, helping both New Space and established organisations set up their operations infrastructure or introduce new ground segment technologies.
In partnership with the European Space Agency (ESA), Starion Luxembourg is leading a consortium of key partners to develop and demonstrate a next-generation operational testbed targeting end-to-end quantum-safe communications. We work to provide operational solutions over fibre and satellite networks in existing national and international environments.
Tasks and activities
The scope of work will include:
Leading the security design of INT-UQKD protocol(s), covering the full stack: physical QKD key generation, resilient secret sharing, and the multiparty key delivery application across distributed communication.
Developing the security models for the cryptographic primitives underpinning the protocol(s), ensuring that their implementation is formally robust against attacks, delivering a key delivery service that aligns with INT-UQKD security and operational requirements.
Collaborating with the system architect to convert the system architecture into clear, technical requirements that enable the development team to implement the protocols securely and reliably.
Skills and experience
The following skills and experience are mandatory:
University Degree or equivalent in a relevant field
Experience in applied cryptography with deep theoretical and practical knowledge of the prevalent cryptographic schemes (QKD, Post- Quantum Cryptography (PQC), Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Threshold schemes (e.g. Shamir’s Secret Sharing).
Ability to design, analyse, and establish formal security proof of complex multi- layered cryptographic protocols against a range of adversities (computational, quantum, insider, etc.).
System engineering experience with the ability to prepare documents following security requirements.
Desire to work both independently and as part of a team, in an international, multicultural environment.
Solution orientated mindset, with customer focused communication skills.
Fluent in English, both written and spoken.
The following skills would be highly desirable.
Experience with Model Based System Engineering (MBSE)
Expertise with operation and / or security assessment of quantum-safe
Experience in project execution following international standards, such as space (ECSS, CCDS, IDSIS), military (MIL-STD, NATO) or regulatory (ETSI, ITU, 3GPP) standards.
Background in creating cybersecurity test plans, performing critical (including space-related) system cybersecurity testing, and analysing test results.
Familiar with monitoring protocols and OS tools, such as SNMP or Syslog.
Expertise in secure software development life cycle (SDLC) principles and practices.
Knowledgeable with automated software deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications (Kubernetes)
Eligibility for NATO and/or EU Security clearances.
Why should you apply?
You will have the opportunity to work within leading space organisations across Europe.
We encourage everyone to think outside the box and to push the boundaries of traditional knowledge. This role is an opportunity to join a forward-thinking company and allows for a deeper understanding of the industry.
To be part of a company that values integrity, inspiration, care and collaboration.
